title: QUIC RFC 9000 DATA_BLOCKED Frame Focused Proof
purpose: Describe the bounded RFC 9000 Section 19.12 DATA_BLOCKED parser, formatter, field-boundary, and benchmark proof slice.
design_summary: The DATA_BLOCKED frame remains centered on the existing span-backed frame codec and immutable frame view. The parser accepts the fixed DATA_BLOCKED frame type 0x14, parses the Maximum Data field as a QUIC variable-length integer, reports the parsed connection-level blocking limit, and consumes exactly the DATA_BLOCKED frame bytes so following packet frames remain available to the packet parser. The formatter writes the fixed type and Maximum Data field through the shared QUIC variable-length integer formatter and rejects values outside the 62-bit varint range.
data_and_state_considerations: This slice is wire-shape proof over QuicDataBlockedFrame.MaximumData and the frame codec. Runtime flow-control emission remains owned by the existing DATA_BLOCKED runtime artifact family; this proof does not introduce new sender scheduling, credit autotuning, or asynchronous wait-state behavior.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Non-0x14 and non-minimal 0x14 frame-type encodings are rejected by the fixed-type parser.
The Maximum Data field is accepted at each QUIC variable-length integer width boundary, including the maximum 62-bit varint value.
Truncated Maximum Data variable-length integers are rejected before a frame view is produced.
Formatter calls reject Maximum Data values above the QUIC variable-length integer range.
The parser consumes only the DATA_BLOCKED frame and leaves any trailing frame bytes for the packet parser.
alternatives_considered: Leave S19P12 under the existing broad frame-codec closeout; rejected because generated triage still reported missing required edge proof for requirements 0003, 0004, and 0006.

Change the DATA_BLOCKED runtime emission policy; rejected because the reported gap is parser and field-shape proof, while runtime emission remains separately traced under the existing Section 4 and Section 19.12 runtime slice.

Add a standalone DATA_BLOCKED benchmark suite; rejected because the existing QuicFrameCodec benchmark suite already owns permanent parser and formatter hot-path coverage for neighboring frame families.
risks: This proof does not claim new DATA_BLOCKED emission scheduling or retry policy.
This proof does not add public flow-control tuning APIs or receiver autotuning behavior.
Malformed-frame handling is proven at the codec seam, not as a hosted endpoint close-packet assertion for every malformed DATA_BLOCKED input.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers RFC 9000 Section 19.12 DATA_BLOCKED type encoding, Maximum Data field varint encoding, field-boundary behavior, and parser/formatter benchmark coverage for requirements 0003, 0004, and 0006 only.
